title: Renowned Explorers: International Society
text: Like many before me I came across this game by accident and liked the look and purchased it on a whim, which turned out to be a good one. It’s an Indiana Jones style turn based exploration game you and your crew travelling around the globe, searching ancient sites in the hopes of finding treasures all the while meeting interested personalities. It’s a light-hearted and humorous game with three different ways of winning encounters direct fighting, hurling insults or charming them with your wit. This is an excellent game and would recommend to anyone, thumbs up!

title: Renowned Explorers: International Society
text: Renowned Explorers: International Society is mostly a turn-based combat Adventure with almost no main or sub plots, you just explore different islands or historical sites and find treasures to reach your goal and that's it, so it is not strictly an RPG because there is not much story. The combat is like the rock-paper-scissors thing where one kind of attack defeats the other, so you actually  have far less choices  than you think to how you want to tackle the situation regardless of your team's strength, which is a very bad thing. It has a lot of different skill rolls to see wether you can successfully complete a random task or not and the prize is either money, fame, or research points, and one of those 3 thing will be used to calculate your total expeditions point called Renown. You win the game with high enough Renown point. This game is awfully childish, the writing, the encounter, the dialogue, awful.I can actually see how this game be a very educational game for younger players, maybe to learn different english words. And the developers, while they are not as imaginative and original as they think they are, is actually a bunch of people full of passion and dreams, but still. you should buy this game only if these two criteria is fulfilled first:First, you have to be very young, most preferably not older than 15 year-old. I am not saying that older men cannot enjoy this game, it is just this game is quite childish, and I am a 34 yo Asian male from a developing country, so I know that my childish might not be your childish(i doubted that), please judge this accordingly. Second, if you decide to buy this, do not buy the whole thing including the DLCs like I did. I bought it all and found out the game is too childish to my liking so I never played the DLC at all. Buy the base game, play it for more than 5 hours(this is very important, you must play it for sufficient amount of time) and then buy the DLC if you still find the game enjoyable.

title: Renowned Explorers: International Society
text: Renowned Explorer (RE) is one of the very best game that I have played for the last 10 years, period :). I have about 300 games, and haven't felt so excited about a new game for such a long time --- perhaps the last time that I felt so excited was  as long as Civilization 1 in 1991. I normally play RPGs, but Renowned Explorer is in a Genre all by itself. It's radically different from the typical RPG or strategy games that I am family with.  Because it is so different, it took me a while to grasp and learn the basics of the game. In the end, after learning about the game, I begin to have great fun... and hundreds of hours on the game. The nice thing about RE is that the entire game campaign consists of 5 expeditions, and you can play it over and over again with different team setups. Different team captains have different super powers, and so, each game with a different captain usually require different strategy and even different playstyle, making in intriguing and interesting. Another nice thing about RE is that the development team offered to add additional contents and updates on a regular basis. So far they have already added quite a bit of new content. Such a commitment from a developing team is really commendable. Even with 276 hours played, I will still be playing this game whenever they add anything new. I am sure I will get MORE than my money's worth and highly recommend this game.

title: Renowned Explorers: International Society

text: I guess my Nostalgia Goggles made me forget how Silly this one really is, it's definately not worth the asking price. I think what made this memerable is that by the time it came out we were all missing that Mansion so much that is seemed better than it really was and I'm sure that the "Zero" stands for Zero Game Immersion.  Suffice it to say that this Offering is a Real Stinker alright feeling as though they released it while still in the BETA Stage. The only good thing to say about this Remaster is that they have done a Stellar job cleaning up the Graphics....Exept that  for some Truly Bizzare reason they have not even bothered with the Cut scenes!  The result could not be more Jarring and More Immersion Breaking, truly Lazy, Lazy programming. The Sound is practically Nonexistent after the Train Stage, and asside from the Sound of your Footsteps and sometimes the Odd sound of Machienary here and there, around 80% of this game is played in Virtual Silence.  There were some good background tunes that were made with this but they were hardly ever used in the finished product. The CO-OP feature was, well, a really bad idea to begin with.  If it had been kept to a Minimum then perhaps it would have worked but as things are you will be spending most of your time in the inventory.  This is by far not only the most Tedius Resident Evil game there is but one of the most Tedius games Ever. The Dialogue Slowly becomes more and more embarresing, so much so that by the Final stage it goes way beyond "Jill Sandwitch" type bad into Full On Scooby-Doo!!  It would have been better if this had been a deliberate Parody but it was done in all seriousness. The Puzzles are completely irrelivant to the story and are just thrown in for something to do (including that awful Three Crate puzzle that made me quit for Three months last time around).  These are just weird random features that you would expect to find on a Big Fish HO game not a Big Budget CAPCOM  Production.  Truly, Truly Weird!! This empty, unfinished Train Wreck of a game has "ZERO" Replayability unless you can take the EMO Wesker Extra.  Sure buy it to be a completeist but for heavens sake wait till it has been substantially discounted.

RE has always been a series where you have to fill in the gaps between what you're doing and what actually happens (unless Jill and Chris are in parallel universes) but Zero is the point where it becomes completely and utterly divorced from reality. If you need more classic RE, definitely pick this up. Just keep in mind there was a good reason why the next game in the series abandoned the formula.

title: Resident Evil 0 / biohazard 0 HD REMASTER
text: First up, my congrats to Capcom for managing to successfully port a GameCube game to Steam! Maybe you learned something from your♥♥♥♥♥♥house RE1 port? Then again, I sincerely hope not, since you've never taken the time to go back and fix that one for the numerous punters for whom it STILL DOES NOT WORK. But let's let bygones be bygones, eh? It was only a few hours of my life which I'll never get back, vainly testing it out on multiple machines. And what's a few hours, out of a whole lifetime? Useless turds. Secondly, I'm giving this game a pretty decent score, but please understand this score comes with reservations. The game has dated somewhat, and was never the very, very best of the RE games in the first place. They've also done such a♥♥♥♥♥♥poor job of updating things like menus and mechanics that I'm not sure how much I can recommend this to anyone who didn't play it the first time 'round. Put it this way: if you're new to not only this but any other old-school, fixed-camera-angle survival horror games, this definitely isn't the place to start. Its mechanics were tricky even back when, what with all the pedantic partner-swapping and ruthless inventory antics, and it's become even less forgiving with time. But for those who have fond if slightly frustrated memories of playing this on the G-Cube...welcome home. You know what to expect. The partner-swapping thing, once you get used to it, was actually one of the niftiest things about the game when it first came out. In short, you have to swap frequently between the cute-but-mousy Rebecca Chambers and the surly-but-sexy Billy Coen in order to successfully solve various puzzles, perform specific tasks, etc. They'll get constantly separated, have to closely co-operate, fight side-by-side whenever possible...you name it, this game gets pretty good mileage out of the partner premise. It's more than just a gimmick, in other words; it's absolutely integral to story and gameplay. That said, it also has its irritations, but...I'll leave it up to you to find those out for yourself. Wouldn't wanna spoil ALL your fun. Another area where this game excels is atmosphere. Like any great horror game, it has fantastic locations, memorable monsters, and there's no denying that the spiffy new graphics look...well, pretty darned spiffy. I just can't warn the unwary enough about the game's overall difficulty and awkwardness, especially early on. You want resource management? Boy, do we have your resource management. The opening couple of hours on the train will test your resource management skills like few games before or since, believe me. You're a better gamer than yours truly if you can manage to procure and/or productively use every item on offer without constantly dropping things and backtracking for them later. For two certifiably butt-kickin' characters, they sure don't seem to be able to carry a lot of stuff between 'em. Useless ♥♥♥♥ers. I still love this game, but a part of me hates it, too. The score below is biased and mostly aimed at veterans, as I've already noted. For everyone else, the risk is yours. Don't say I didn't warn you. Verdict: 8.5/10 (9 for the game, minus 0.5 for the lazy port).

title: Resident Evil 0 / biohazard 0 HD REMASTER
text: Resident Evil Zero was originally released on Gamecube in 2002, and was also ported to the Wii in 2008. I never played either of those versions, which means I can't really comment on how faithful this HD remake is, so I will simply judge this version on its own merits. On the whole I enjoyed playing the game, although it does have some problems. As the name suggests, Zero is a prequel to RE1. There are two playable characters, STARS member Rebecca, and convicted criminal Billy. The player can switch between them at will, with the AI controlling the other character, or you can explore with one character on their own. Billy has more health, is strong enough to move heavy objects, and has a cigarette lighter, whilst Rebecca can mix herbs and other chemicals. Gameplay contains both the good and the bad of old school survival horror. Combat is a slower pace, there are a small number of monsters, but each one is dangerous. Resource management is key, because ammo and healing items are scarce, so you can't afford to waste any. Puzzles are intelligently designed to require both characters working together. Unfortunately the fixed camera angles are far more annoying than I remember in RE1. There is a ridiculous number of combat encounters where the monster is off screen, my character is looking at the monster, but I can't see what they see, because I'm forced to look at my character, which makes aiming more difficult than it should be. Thankfully the partner AI is pretty useful, although I'm not sure if "standing still while the AI shoots the monsters" qualifies as playing the game. I'm so glad later games in the franchise dropped the fixed camera angles. Most of the boss fights are frustrating, because they always disable one character during a cutscene, meaning you can't access their inventory. I always died on the first attempt just because I ran out of ammo, having split my ammo between the two characters. On my second attempt, armed with advanced knowledge of what is about to happen, I gave all my weapons/ammo to the character who wouldn't be disabled and got an easy kill. I don't mind dying in games if I make a mistake, but this felt "cheap". This game has the same mouse pointer bug that the RE1 HD remake had. If you play with mouse and keyboard, the mouse pointer will constantly be visible on screen. The only solution is to play with a gamepad and push the mouse pointer off screen. Fortunately the controls work well with a gamepad, but I don't understand why Capcom are having so much difficulty figuring out how a mouse works. Ultimately I think you need to be an existing fan of the Resident Evil franchise, and be willing to overlook some problems, to enjoy RE Zero. If you've never played Resident Evil before, I would recommend starting with better games such as RE1, or RE Revelations 1 &2, and then grab Zero if you find yourself wanting more.

title: Reus
text: I think Reus is a very elegant god-game simplified down to a very fun level. Some people like the ability to actually influence specific citizens or creatures, I prefer the Reus approach where the little factors all are automatic and you just make big decisions. Some people also prefer an open-ended game, while I prefer the goal oriented design of Reus. You can play for as long as you want even after the era ends so I'm not sure why some people complain about it. I am rather confused on why many reviews call it a puzzle game. Yes, you have certain objectives meaning you need to structure your cities in a certain way, but it doesn't pigeon-hole you into a puzzle by any stretch. For instance lets say you need 100 food to make a farm - you could plant some bushes, or you could make your grassland an ocean and make fish, or you could put chickens by your bushes, etc. Or you can choose to destroy the farm and make something else. The tech tree is quite substantial and there are countless ways to build each city. This is no more a puzzle than making a research centric city in Civilization. You build the things that boost that one aspect and reduce the others. Perhaps you need to make more trade-offs in Reus and people don't like that? The only criticism I have is that after you unlock everything the game is kind of boring. 8/10

title: Reus
text: I normally don't like any civilization-building or strategy type games, but I really liked this. I was drawn to it because of the art, it just looked so pretty and it was on sale! I love games where there are a huge number of achievements and possibilities. This game is great. Visually, it is very nice and calming, though simple. You control 4 giants that control different aspects of life on the planet; for example, the Rock Giant can create mountains and deserts, ore mines, can give upgrades to a few different parts of the game, and can destroy villages with earthquakes. (Other giants are swamp, forest, and ocean) You have to create a balance...two of the giants can give different types of animals, two can give different plants, and one can give ores/minerals. Each land type (swamp, forest, ocean, desert, and mountain) creates different options for what resource can be placed, and each resource gives off a different reward (wealth, food, technology, danger, etc.) (Example - you can use the Ocean Giant's animal resource in the forest and get a chicken or swamp for a frog (each area has a different outcome.)) Placing certain things beside each other will, also, give special rewards. You can use the upgrades from each giant to transform the resource into a better and different one that may give off different rewards. As you build up your planet, humans will settle and begin building villages. As they become more prosperous, they start trying to build shrines, churches, trade markets, schools, etc. Each one requires a certain amount of wealth, food, etc so you have to carefully plan out where to place everything for the most reward in a small space. There is a time limit, you can open longer times as you play. You can also unlock new animals, plants, ores, achievements, etc. If you don't get the balance right, the village may not thrive. If the village becomes to prosperous, it may cause wars against each other, or even against the giants themselves. This game can be maddening and overwhelming, especially when you are still a low level, but it really fun and rewarding when you accomplish your goals. I enjoy playing it when I just need to relax or, maybe, take out some villages with some swamp slime.
